key_insight: Corner vortices in slow triangular-cavity flow form a self-similar cascade whose sizes, strengths, and fractal dimensions follow systematic scaling laws.
engineering_relevance: These scaling relations help predict near-corner flow structure in viscous cavity flows, which is useful for microfluidics, mixing, and corner-dominated transport design.
method: Solved incompressible Navier–Stokes equations numerically with a pressure-based coupled solver.
Quantified successive vortices using size and intensity ratios in the spirit of Moffatt corner-vortex theory.
Estimated fractal dimension with the area–perimeter method and proposed an empirical predictor across grid resolutions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical results showing non-integer fractal dimensions between 1 and 2, with systematic dependence on vortex size, intensity, Reynolds number, and cavity geometry.
watch_item: The fractal estimates depend on grid resolution and vortex identification, so coarse meshes or inconsistent segmentation may bias the inferred scaling.
paper_title: Fractal Scaling of Moffatt Vortices in Triangular Cavity Flow
